reasons: Compile OK. Trigger NodeUtilTest::testGetVarsDeclaredInBranch fails with expected:<[]> but was:<[foo]> (input 'function(){var foo;}'). The full variant suite fails only the trigger, and the three ownership tests pass. (a) The gold is the only method on the path that computes anything: it alone walks the tree and decides, node by node, whether to record a name and whether to descend. On the trigger it records foo, a var of the nested anonymous function. That is not a var declared in the branch, given the facade's 'excluding descent scopes', the production caller's 'not in an inner scope' and SyntacticScopeCreator.scanVars. Hops 1-4 are pure pass-throughs, so their outputs are wrong only by inheritance. (b) Each hop's javadoc matches its body: insertion-ordered map, pass-through, 'first declaration'. All share the gold's contract wording, and none promises a step it could own. (c) Four non-gold repairs were run through the trigger, the ownership tests and the full suite. All four pass, but none is a competing repair. The one-line hop-4 child loop is an overfit that still enters functions nested two or more levels deep and a FUNCTION root, so it breaks the facade's contract. A post-filter at hop 1 or the facade loses the branch's own var when an inner function declares the same name first, because the gold keeps first declarations. A write-filtering map at hop 2 and a visitPreOrder re-walk at hop 4 are bypasses: they override or replace the gold's decision or walk. The declared compensating edits all still fail the trigger. (d) Neutral names (getDeclaredVars, declaredVarMap, addVarDeclarations, gatherVarDecls, addBranchVars) and no fault vocabulary. The variant gold reads as an ordinary 'if NAME record, else recurse'. The lie ('flattened level by level ... sorted alphabetically') is a false procedure; it names neither functions nor scopes nor the skipped descent. (e) The gold is exactly 5 calls below the facade. Hosts are 5 distinct existing classes: Node, Parser, TokenStream, TypeCheck, Compiler.CodeBuilder. The facade is one delegating call (the original had no guard) and carries one added false procedural sentence; there is no level-order flattening and no sort, and order is pre-order first declaration. The gold's javadoc is silent on functions and scopes. The trigger is an existing test and the only new failure. (f) The convention is pinned outside the gold: by SyntacticScopeCreator.scanVars ('should not examine function's children'); by the javadoc of NodeUtil.redeclareVarsInsideBranch ('not in an inner scope'); by the facade's original 'excluding descent scopes'; and by passing tests: SyntacticScopeCreatorTest.testFunctionScope (y in a nested function is not declared globally) and FoldConstantsTest.testVarLifting ('if(false)var a=function(){var b};' lifts only a).
notes: Residual interpretive point. The gold's and hops' shared phrase 'vars declared in a branch' could be read literally as every var whose declaration appears anywhere in the subtree. Under that reading only the facade ('excluding descent scopes') would be violated. Even then, no small non-bypass facade or hop repair exists, because first-declaration-wins makes post-filtering unrecoverable (demonstrated above). The pins and the production caller make the scope-aware reading the natural one, so I do not consider ownership genuinely arguable. Weak pins: testVarLifting passes on the variant too, because the gold never descends into a NAME's initializer, so it pins the convention but does not discriminate. testRemovalRequiresRedeclaration pins redeclaration, not function exclusion. testFunctionScope exercises the sibling SyntacticScopeCreator, not the chain. The existing suite also accepts the one-line hop-4 overfit (full suite clean), because only the trigger probes function exclusion, and only with depth-1 functions. Cosmetic transform artifacts: the facade's lie line lacks the javadoc ' * ' prefix and the body is indented 8 spaces; hop 4's javadoc is misindented; TokenStream (rhino) now imports jscomp.TypeCheck. None of them points at the gold. The correct patch matched the pristine VarCollector implementation on all 14 probe inputs. Scratch: /private/tmp/mxb-NMEtcF (deleted after the audit).
